rule: Separator lines partition the grid into (possibly non-rectangular) regions; each region is filled with concentric rings following its boundary, cycling the colours given by the seed cells placed diagonally in a region corner.
gap: Needs ring code = distance to the boundary of each separator-delimited irregular region, with per-region colour cycle read from corner seeds.

rule: From a start marker on the grid edge draw a staircase path rightwards/upwards that turns whenever it would leave the current colour region, writing the repeating colour sequence shown in the top-left legend and ending with the legend's terminal colour; legend and end markers are erased.
gap: Needs a turning path-following behaviour (turn on region boundary) plus reading a colour sequence from a legend to paint along the path.

rule: Large colour regions carry small 1-coloured arrow glyphs holding a colour cell; each arrow paints the region it points into with its carried colour, glyphs are removed, regions are cleaned to rectangles and the whole grid is rotated 90 degrees.
gap: Needs arrow glyphs interpreted as pointers carrying a colour into a neighbouring region, plus region-level recolouring and global rotation chained.

rule: Black-framed boxes of 5/7 cells attached to 9-coloured rails slide along the rail (toward the far 9 stop) and each step of travel converts one 5 into 7, so displacement equals the number of newly filled 7 cells (progress-bar).
gap: Needs coupled slide-and-fill behaviour: move box along rail to a stop while converting cells, with travel distance tied to a cell count.

rule: Collect the 4x4 squares, split them into hollow and solid, sort each list by vertical position, and stack them in a two-column output (hollow left, solid right), padding with black.
gap: Needs object-list sorting by position, partition by hollow/solid, and assembling an output grid from multiple selected objects rather than one.

rule: Two symmetric creature-like objects: a multicoloured one and a plain outline template of different size; output is the coloured object non-uniformly stretched (rows/columns duplicated or shifted) to fit the template's silhouette and bounding box.
gap: Needs non-rigid deformation: stretching an object's rows/columns to match another object's outline, beyond D8 transforms and uniform scaling.

rule: A black k x k block travels through the blue maze corridor toward the red k x k block; it ends at the red block if the corridor is wide enough all the way, otherwise at the last position before the corridor narrows below k; its start cells become blue.
gap: Needs path search of a k x k block through the maze toward a target, stopping where the corridor narrows; dynamics only moves straight.

rule: Scattered jigsaw fragments (pieces of a bordered rectangular picture) are translated so that they fit together into one complete framed rectangle, anchored at the largest/anchor piece; everything else is erased.
gap: Needs jigsaw assembly: search over piece placements so edges/borders match into a single complete rectangle.

rule: Inside each black rectangular frame, a coloured marker near a corner marks that corner: the marker colour is put on the inner corner cell and a small L-shaped bracket of that colour is drawn hugging the frame's outer corner.
gap: Needs part-level rule: map each marker to its nearest frame corner and draw a corner-oriented bracket there, whatever the marker offset.

rule: Unclear: separator-split panels contain noise pixels plus one small shape recurring in different poses/positions; the output is a single panel showing only that shape in one pose at a position seemingly anchored to pixels common to all panels (test has a single panel).
gap: Needs recognising a recurring shape under noise and pose change across panels and inferring its output pose/location; panel voting fails because shapes move.

rule: A red beam shoots from the 4-tipped start marker; every blob it enters turns red and re-emits the beam (with the 3-marker's width) in the direction its green 3-marker points, chaining through blobs; untouched blobs are erased.
gap: Needs a ray that is redirected by objects: object-specific exit direction read from a marker side, chained across hits, with unhit objects deleted.

rule: The top panels hold k x k tile patterns and the bottom row gives each panel a colour key; a small layout map (in key colours) is expanded so each map cell becomes the k x k pattern bound to its colour, drawn in that colour.
gap: Needs binding pattern panels to colour keys and a map-driven fractal substitution: each map cell replaced by the pattern its colour denotes.

rule: Crop the large square concentric object (dropping the small stray pieces) and rotate its nested layers by different amounts (e.g. outer frame by 90 degrees, inner rings by 180), keeping the centre motif.
gap: Needs part-wise transforms: decompose an object into nested rings and apply a different rotation to each, after cropping it.

rule: The separator-delimited 5x5 panels are re-laid out as a single strip (vertical for 2D/horizontal inputs, horizontal for vertical inputs) in the order that makes each panel's line pattern connect to the next one at the shared edge.
gap: Needs re-arranging panels into a chain by matching edge contact points (a consistent ordering search), not voting/overlaying panels.

rule: Straight lines have gaps and some short diagonal stray segments; a gap is bridged (filled in line colour) when a displaced diagonal fragment of matching length sits next to it, and all diagonal fragments are erased; other gaps stay open.
gap: Needs pairing diagonal stray fragments with same-length line gaps (selective connect) and deleting the fragments; plain connect fills every gap.

rule: On a checkerboard, a diamond object has coloured diagonal edge segments; each segment is extruded outward (perpendicular to itself, away from the diamond) as a pair of diagonal stripes from its end cells to the grid border.
gap: Needs extruding each edge segment along its outward normal (direction set by its side of the object), from segment endpoints on checkerboard parity.

rule: Overlapping rectangle outlines of different colours are each divided into compartments by inner lines; output has one row per rectangle colour with bar length equal to its compartment count, rows sorted by count, padded with the noise colour.
gap: Needs counting enclosed compartments per (occluded) outline colour and rendering sorted count bars; no counting/sorting output generator exists.

rule: Each object is made left-right mirror symmetric about its best vertical axis by deleting the few cells that have no mirror partner.
gap: Self-model needs per-object symmetry with axis search, and repair by deletion (intersect with mirror) instead of filling occluded cells.

rule: Vertical bars have caps of a colour; a top-left legend gives, per cap colour, a vertical run of length k; the k-th tallest bar with that cap colour has its interior recoloured to the cap colour.
gap: Needs ranking same-cap bars by height and reading k from the legend run length per colour; pattern module only copies local looks.

rule: On a periodic background there are two framed boxes: one holds complete small motifs, the other only their key cells; output is the second box cropped with each key cell expanded into the matching motif copied from the first box.
gap: Needs chaining crop-the-sparse-box with in-grid template stamping: match key cells to motifs found in another box and paste them around keys.

rule: Solid 3x3 coloured squares are wired by 8-lines (5 marks crossings where wires pass over each other) to free terminals; each square turns into a hollow plus of its colour and an X-shape of that colour appears at the terminal its wire leads to.
gap: Needs tracing wires straight through crossing marks to find each square's terminal, then shape substitution (solid square to plus, X at endpoint).

rule: Four separator panels give a shape, a set of small green blobs, and two colours; output repeats the shape N times (N = number of green blobs) along the strip axis, drawn in the first colour on the second colour with one-cell gaps.
gap: Needs repetition count taken from the number of objects in a panel, combined with panel-role binding for shape and colours; tiling factors are fixed.

rule: A lattice of identical 3x3 tiles has a few tiles replaced by a special tile; complete the replacement so that, at the tile level, the special tiles form a 3x3 arrangement shaped like the special tile's own foreground pattern (self-similar), aligned with the existing partial placement.
gap: Needs hierarchical self-similar completion: infer tile-level layout equal to the tile's pattern and locate it consistently with the partial instances.

rule: Copies of one composite object appear at several scales in two variants (different colours of some parts, cap or foot part present/absent); every instance is converted to the other variant, keeping its scale.
gap: Needs scale-invariant part matching across object instances and a variant swap (A to B, B to A), including adding/removing parts; association needs same-scale templates.

rule: A top-left key box lists a set of colours; every black box whose scattered cells include all key colours is erased (filled with the background 7), other boxes are kept.
gap: Needs a set-containment test between each box's colour set and a key's colour set to decide deletion; no such relational predicate exists.

rule: Pairs of 1-cells on a common diagonal are joined by a diagonal 1-line; each 6-cell lying on such a connector shoots a 6-line along the perpendicular diagonal in both directions to the borders (overwriting); other 6s stay.
gap: Needs chaining diagonal connect with conditional perpendicular diagonal rays fired only by 6s lying on a connector line.

rule: Each 2x2 coloured core sits in a green frame with gaps; through every gap a ray of the core colour is emitted outward (straight for side gaps, diagonal for corner gaps) and runs to the border, deflecting/stopping at other objects.
gap: Needs rays whose direction is set per gap by its position relative to the core (8 directions), emitted only through frame openings.

rule: The top legend maps each block colour to a turn (left/right, shown by where the colour bar sits in its box); the 8 seed extends as a 2-wide line that turns as the legend dictates whenever it hits a coloured block, until leaving the grid; legend is cropped away.
gap: Needs a bouncing/turning line behaviour whose turn direction at each obstacle is looked up from a colour-to-direction legend.

rule: The grid has four quadrants: a holey pattern, a filler pattern and two shape/size cues; the holes (0) of the pattern are filled from the filler pattern and the result is tiled to an output size seemingly given by the other quadrants' extents or counts.
gap: Needs chaining panel overlay (fill holes from another panel) with tiling whose repeat counts are inferred from other panels' sizes/counts; exact size rule unclear.
